name: infantry_list_sessions
description: List the SESSIONS (running or past agent runs, not saved profiles) the Infantry AI daemon knows: id, agentId, role, provider, model, projectId, status.

projectId.description: Only this project's sessions. Omitted: a session caller's own project (everyone else: all). "all" lists every project (pm / owner callers only).

name: infantry_get_session
description: One session's status and the last lines of its transcript (from the daemon's replay buffer, bounded).

sessionId.description: Session id, or a unique prefix of one.

brief.description: Omit the transcript: return only state, live state, last action and last output/event times.

lines.description: How many trailing transcript lines to return.

name: infantry_pod_state
description: Summary of the pod: saved PROFILES (templates, not running) grouped by role under `agents`, SESSIONS by status; optionally one project's `roster` (its live AGENTS, BUSY/IDLE/OFFLINE: who can be assigned work) and one pod's node state.

projectId.description: Include this project's live roster (running agents, not profiles: agent, role, BUSY/IDLE/OFFLINE). Default: the caller's own project; "all" (pm / owner callers only) covers every project.

podId.description: Include this pod's state and nodes.

name: infantry_board
description: The board in one call: tickets grouped by column (backlog, todo, in_progress, pending, done), one line each with its worker (role, session id), the worker's live state (busy / idle / running background process), last action, last output age, branch and last commit. Use this instead of tickets + sessions + transcripts.

projectId.description: Project whose tickets to summarise. Default: the caller's own project; "all" (pm / owner callers only) covers every project, each line prefixed [projectId].

name: infantry_spawn
description: Spawn an Infantry AI session for a role and/or an agent profile, optionally sending it a first task, OUTSIDE the board: it runs in the project folder and leaves every ticket untouched. Never use it for ticket work: start ticket work with infantry_ticket_start (or pass ticketId here, which does the same), so the worker runs the ticket's role, provider and model on its own ticket branch and the ticket goes In Progress. Guarded: refused beyond the MCP spawn depth limit and beyond this server's open-session limit.

role.description: Role to spawn (role-first, like the `new` frame).

agentId.description: Agent profile id; with role, it must be that profile's role.

projectId.description: Project the session belongs to (default: the server's --project / .infantry/mcp.json projectId).

task.description: Optional first prompt for the new session.

contextLimit.description: Context limit for the session in tokens (200000, 200k, 1m; off = none, the default): a larger one for a hard, long task, a smaller one for a small job. How it is honoured depends on the harness: infantry_list_harnesses shows contextLimit per harness (supported / best_effort / unsupported; unsupported = recorded, not applied).

effort.description: Reasoning effort for the session: low, medium, high, xhigh or max (off = the harness default, the default). How it is honoured depends on the harness: infantry_list_harnesses shows effort per harness (supported / best_effort / unsupported; unsupported = recorded, not applied).

runner.description: Where the session runs: local, a paired runner name, or any. Over the agent profile's runner, under a ticket pin; an unknown, down, paused or full runner refuses the spawn (no silent local fallback).

provider.description: Harness (provider id) the session runs, as the app's Start box picks it: see infantry_list_harnesses. Omitted = the agent profile, the role's binding, then the project's routing rules. An unknown provider refuses the spawn.

model.description: Model id of that harness (infantry_list_harnesses lists them); a model the provider does not list refuses the spawn.

toolApproval.description: This session's own Tool approval: ask (approval cards in the app), deny, allowEdits or allowAll. Omitted = the global setting.

ticketId.description: Start this board ticket instead (full id or its 8-char suffix), exactly as infantry_ticket_start: the ticket's own role, provider, model and description apply, so role / agentId / projectId must agree with it and task is refused.

detail.description: How much to send back: ack (tiny), summary (compact), full. Default: the tool's own, or setting limits.mcp.defaultDetail.

maxChars.description: Cut this call's result at this many characters (default: setting limits.mcp.maxResultChars).

name: infantry_prompt
description: Send a prompt to an existing session (id or unique prefix). Slash commands are refused.

sessionId.description: Session id, or a unique prefix of one.

prompt.description: The words to send to the agent.

detail.description: How much to send back: ack (tiny), summary (compact), full. Default: the tool's own, or setting limits.mcp.defaultDetail.

maxChars.description: Cut this call's result at this many characters (default: setting limits.mcp.maxResultChars).

name: infantry_message
description: Send Infantry AI COMMS mail to an agent id, a role (of the sender's project) or a session id.

to.description: Recipient: agent id, role, or session id.

allowCrossProject.description: Send even though the recipient is in another project (refused by default).

name: infantry_kill
description: Kill a session (id or unique prefix). A pm (or the owner) may kill any session in its own project; other roles only sessions they spawned. To kill AND remove a stuck session in one call, use infantry_session_remove with force=true.

sessionId.description: Session id, or a unique prefix of one.

force.description: Kill the process tree at once instead of after the grace period.

detail.description: How much to send back: ack (tiny), summary (compact), full. Default: the tool's own, or setting limits.mcp.defaultDetail.

maxChars.description: Cut this call's result at this many characters (default: setting limits.mcp.maxResultChars).

name: infantry_session_remove
description: Remove an ended (exited, failed or orphaned) session from the session list, which is what the sidebar shows. With force=true a running (BUSY / idle) session is killed first, then removed, in one call (same scope rule as infantry_kill). Without force a running session is refused. Any ended session may be removed, role agents included. Keeps the ticket, the runs history, the branch and worktree, and mail; the removed session can no longer be resumed.

sessionId.description: Session id, or a unique prefix of one.

force.description: Kill the session first if it is running, then remove it.

detail.description: How much to send back: ack (tiny), summary (compact), full. Default: the tool's own, or setting limits.mcp.defaultDetail.

maxChars.description: Cut this call's result at this many characters (default: setting limits.mcp.maxResultChars).

name: infantry_session_restart
description: Reboot a session in place: same id, role, harness, model, project and worktree, a fresh agent process whose first prompt is composed anew (role notes, project notes, identity). Refused while the session is mid-turn unless force is true, which kills the running turn's process tree and restarts.

sessionId.description: Session id, or a unique prefix of one.

force.description: Kill the process tree at once instead of after the grace period.

detail.description: How much to send back: ack (tiny), summary (compact), full. Default: the tool's own, or setting limits.mcp.defaultDetail.

maxChars.description: Cut this call's result at this many characters (default: setting limits.mcp.maxResultChars).

name: infantry_ticket_create
description: Create a ticket on the Infantry AI board (it lands in todo, the current sprint, or in backlog with status backlog; nothing runs until infantry_ticket_start starts it, and a backlog ticket is never started). The description is stored verbatim, multi-line included. role / provider / model pin who runs it (infantry_list_harnesses lists the provider ids and their models); the daemon refuses an unknown provider or a model that provider does not list. The answer says what was saved.

description.description: Full brief, Markdown, any number of lines; stored exactly as given.

projectId.description: Project the ticket belongs to (default: this session's project).

role.description: Role that runs it (stored as role:<id>), e.g. backend.

provider.description: Harness (provider id) that runs it, e.g. claude or opencode: see infantry_list_harnesses.

model.description: Model pin, one of that harness's models: see infantry_list_harnesses.

weight.description: Ticket weight 1-5 by how likely the ticket is to come back wrong, not its size: 4-5 wire/contract, daemon, auth or project scope, concurrency/SSR timing, Android build, or more than one module; 3 gate fixes, bisects, UI that depends on daemon behaviour; 1-2 copy, icons, renames, docs (mechanical, one owner file). 0 clears it on update. With no provider/model pin the ticket starts on the project's first matching routing rule (project_config routingRules), else the weight mapping (tickets.weightExecutors); an explicit pin always wins. Set a weight on every ticket before start.

contextLimit.description: Context limit for the session in tokens (200000, 200k, 1m; off = none, the default): a larger one for a hard, long task, a smaller one for a small job. How it is honoured depends on the harness: infantry_list_harnesses shows contextLimit per harness (supported / best_effort / unsupported; unsupported = recorded, not applied). Shown on the ticket as effectiveContextLimit (source ticket / default); off clears it on update.

effort.description: Reasoning effort for the ticket's worker: low, medium, high, xhigh or max (off = the harness default, the default); a hard ticket gets a higher one. How it is honoured depends on the harness: infantry_list_harnesses shows effort per harness (supported / best_effort / unsupported; unsupported = recorded, not applied). Shown on the ticket as effectiveEffort (source ticket / rule / agent / role / default); off clears it on update.

images.description: Images to attach: local image file paths (png, jpeg, gif or webp, at most 10 MB each; each is uploaded to the project's .infantry/uploads/ticket/), or paths already stored there. A missing, oversized or non-image file refuses the call and nothing is saved. The board shows them as attachments and the started worker's brief lists them.

status.description: Column the new ticket enters: todo (default, the current sprint) or backlog (parked, never started until moved to todo).

relatedTo.description: Ticket ids (full or 8-char) this ticket relates to: stored as relates_to links, listed first in the RELATED (auto) block the daemon writes atop the description and in the worker's start brief. On update, [] links nothing and rebuilds that block (the `ticket related --suggest` of the CLI).

name: infantry_ticket_update
description: Edit ONE ticket (full id or the 8-char id `tickets` prints). A field left out keeps its stored value; the description, when given, replaces the stored one verbatim. Set role / provider / model here BEFORE infantry_ticket_start: a start runs what the ticket holds. The answer says what was saved.

ticketId.description: Full ticket id, or its 8-char suffix.

description.description: New full description, stored exactly as given.

role.description: Role that runs it (stored as role:<id>).

model.description: Model pin, one of that harness's models: see infantry_list_harnesses.

weight.description: Ticket weight 1-5 by how likely the ticket is to come back wrong, not its size: 4-5 wire/contract, daemon, auth or project scope, concurrency/SSR timing, Android build, or more than one module; 3 gate fixes, bisects, UI that depends on daemon behaviour; 1-2 copy, icons, renames, docs (mechanical, one owner file). 0 clears it on update. With no provider/model pin the ticket starts on the project's first matching routing rule (project_config routingRules), else the weight mapping (tickets.weightExecutors); an explicit pin always wins. Set a weight on every ticket before start.

contextLimit.description: Context limit for the session in tokens (200000, 200k, 1m; off = none, the default): a larger one for a hard, long task, a smaller one for a small job. How it is honoured depends on the harness: infantry_list_harnesses shows contextLimit per harness (supported / best_effort / unsupported; unsupported = recorded, not applied). Shown on the ticket as effectiveContextLimit (source ticket / default); off clears it on update.

effort.description: Reasoning effort for the ticket's worker: low, medium, high, xhigh or max (off = the harness default, the default); a hard ticket gets a higher one. How it is honoured depends on the harness: infantry_list_harnesses shows effort per harness (supported / best_effort / unsupported; unsupported = recorded, not applied). Shown on the ticket as effectiveEffort (source ticket / rule / agent / role / default); off clears it on update.

images.description: The ticket's full image list, replacing the stored one ([] removes all): local image files (uploaded, as for infantry_ticket_create) or paths already under the project's .infantry/uploads/ticket/. Not with addImages / removeImages. A removed image's file is deleted once no ticket references it.

addImages.description: Images to ADD to the stored list: local image files (png, jpeg, gif or webp, at most 10 MB each) or stored paths.

relatedTo.description: Ticket ids (full or 8-char) this ticket relates to: stored as relates_to links, listed first in the RELATED (auto) block the daemon writes atop the description and in the worker's start brief. On update, [] links nothing and rebuilds that block (the `ticket related --suggest` of the CLI).

removeImages.description: Images to REMOVE from the stored list, each named by its stored path (as infantry_ticket_get answers it), its file name, or the original local file. Naming an image the ticket does not have refuses the call.

name: infantry_ticket_start
description: Start ONE ticket: THE way to put an agent to work on a ticket. It is the board's own start (the card moving to In Progress): the worker runs the ticket's role, provider and model, in its own git worktree on branch ticket/<short-id>-<slug>, and the ticket goes In Progress with you recorded as its starter. Pin role / provider / model first with infantry_ticket_create or infantry_ticket_update. A ticket whose lane is busy is queued; one held by open prerequisites, or that cannot start, is refused with the reason. Starting a ticket already in progress returns its worker. Guarded like infantry_spawn.

ticketId.description: Full ticket id, or its 8-char suffix.

name: infantry_epic_base
description: Read, set or clear ONE epic's base branch: new tickets in the epic cut their branch from it, overriding the project's base. A branch that does not resolve where tickets are cut is refused with the reason. Tickets already started keep their recorded base.

branch.description: Branch to set; omit (with clear unset) to read.

clear.description: true removes the setting; the epic's tickets fall back to the project's base.

name: infantry_ticket_delete
description: Delete ONE ticket from the board (full id or the 8-char id `tickets` prints), with its links. An unknown or ambiguous id is refused and nothing is deleted. A ticket in progress is refused: stop its worker first. One ticket per call; there is no bulk delete. The answer names the deleted ticket's id and title.

ticketId.description: Full ticket id, or its 8-char suffix.

name: infantry_ticket_move
description: Move ONE ticket to a status (full id or 8-char id), e.g. done when your work is finished, or todo, or backlog (parked: never started until moved back to todo), and/or reorder it: ticket order inside a column is priority (the board and `tickets` list it top first). Give at most one of before / after (just above / below that ticket), top, bottom or position (0 = top); with one of them the status may be left out and the ticket is reordered in its own column. Same as `infantry ticket move [status] --before|--after|--top|--bottom|--position`. To START a ticket use infantry_ticket_start; pending is set by the daemon from open prerequisites and is refused here. The answer reads back the stored ticket and its position (0 = top).

ticketId.description: Full ticket id, or its 8-char suffix.

status.description: Target status, e.g. done, todo, backlog. Optional when before, top or bottom is given.

before.description: Place the ticket just above this ticket (full id or 8-char suffix), which must be in the target column.

after.description: Place the ticket just below this ticket (full id or 8-char suffix), which must be in the target column.

top.description: Place the ticket at the top of the column (highest priority).

bottom.description: Place the ticket at the bottom of the column.

position.description: Place the ticket at this index of the column, 0 = the top (past the end = the bottom).

name: infantry_inbox
description: List the Infantry AI COMMS mail addressed to you (this session, or the human handle outside one): id, from, subject, state, read, and a one-line preview, oldest first. Read one in full with infantry_read.

unreadOnly.description: Only the messages not read yet.

name: infantry_read
description: Read one message of your inbox in full (its body) and mark it read.

messageId.description: Message id from infantry_inbox, or a unique prefix of one.

name: infantry_pipeline
description: Read the project's verification pipeline: its stages, each commit's current stage (who moved it, when, evidence), and the running checks. configured:false when the project has no pipeline.

name: infantry_pipeline_record
description: Report pipeline state instead of being asked by mail: move a commit to a stage (commit + stage + optional evidence), or start / ping / finish the running check (check + scope; start also needs commit + what).

stage.description: One of the project's configured stage names.

check.description: start, ping or finish: act on the running check instead of a stage.

scope.description: The worktree / build dir the check runs in; empty for the default.

name: infantry_progress
description: Report how far along YOUR long job is (a gate, a build, a download); it shows as a live bar on your card and the PM reads it in infantry_list_sessions. Prefer checkpoints (mode plan with step names, then mode step as each completes) or a counter (mode count, done/total); percent when the tool prints one; status (indeterminate, label only) when nothing can be measured. Never invent a number. done / fail end it. For output streams use the CLI: infantry run --label x -- <cmd>, with ##infantry marker lines.

label.description: What the job is; mode fail: the reason.

steps.description: mode plan: the checkpoint names, in order.

count.description: mode plan: a bare number of checkpoints.

step.description: mode step: the step that just completed (omit = the current one).

total.description: mode bytes / count: the total (omit = unknown).

estimate.description: mode status: show '~N min left (estimated)' from past runs of this label. Last resort only, when nothing can be measured.

name: infantry_watch_file
description: Watch a file another process writes (a build sent to a log with > or tee): you are mailed when it goes quiet, prints a watched pattern (BUILD FAILED, e: ...), runs long, or is done (the process untilPid exited, or the file stopped growing for idleSeconds). Only appended bytes are read, never a copy. Start it, then end your turn; no sleep, no polling.

idleSeconds.description: No pid: done once the file has not grown this long (default limits.watch.fileIdleSeconds).
